requirement:
# REQ-2234: The analyzer does not work if SuppressSourceGeneration = true

Source: https://github.com/MessagePack-CSharp/MessagePack-CSharp/issues/2234

#### Bug description

The analyzer does not work if SuppressSourceGeneration = true. This has happened since version 3.1.1. It still worked in 3.1.0.

story.summary: The agent changed the shared member-collection code in TypeCollector so it no longer crashes on invalid key layouts. For mixed int/string keys, it now reports the diagnostic and skips the member (`continue`). For duplicate int or string keys, it guards each `Dictionary.Add` with `ContainsKey`. It adds analyzer tests for `[MessagePackObject(SuppressSourceGeneration = true)]` types, execution tests showing such a type gets no generated formatter and still round-trips at run time, and a README section describing which diagnostics apply to suppressed types.
story.why: Issue #2234 says the analyzer stopped reporting diagnostics for SuppressSourceGeneration types in 3.1.1. The visible fix implies the root cause was an exception thrown while collecting members with duplicate or mixed keys, which kills the analyzer. However, nothing in the diff touches SuppressSourceGeneration-specific logic. The reviewer cannot confirm from the diff alone that this is the 3.1.0 → 3.1.1 regression rather than a separate crash.
touches_beyond_requirement: The TypeCollector changes apply to every [MessagePackObject] type, including ones that do get a generated formatter, not only suppressed types.
A new README section documents analyzer behavior for suppressed types, including which rules are and are not reported.
Execution tests check run-time round-tripping and that no generated formatter exists; this is beyond the analyzer bug.
story.confidence_overview: Medium that the crash-avoidance edits are correct for the duplicate and mixed-key cases; the new tests cover these. Low-to-medium that this is the whole fix for the reported regression: the diff shows no change to any SuppressSourceGeneration branch. It is unclear whether tests such as MemberWithoutKeyIsReported would have failed before the change. High that the new tests exist and assert specific diagnostics.

claims.text: When a member's key kind (int vs string) differs from the other members, TypeCollector reports DoNotMixStringAndIntKeys and skips that member instead of continuing with a null key. This applies in both member-collection paths (properties and fields).
claims.requirement_quote: The analyzer does not work if SuppressSourceGeneration = true.

claims.text: A duplicate int or string key no longer causes Dictionary.Add to throw. The second member with the same key is not added; the existing duplicate-key diagnostic is expected to have been reported earlier.
claims.requirement_quote: The analyzer does not work if SuppressSourceGeneration = true.

breaker.reason: All three named tests (SuppressSourceGenerationAnalyzerTests.cs lines 81-100, 103-122, and 147-166) declare only properties and no fields, so none of them test the cited field-collection guards at TypeCollector.cs lines 1163-1166 and 1179-1182; furthermore, the earlier duplicate-key diagnostic reporting for intMembers and fields is outside the diff hunks and unverified for fields.

claims.text: Scope: the TypeCollector edits are not limited to suppressed types. They change collection for every MessagePackObject type, including generated ones. No public API, rule descriptor or wire-format code is changed.

breaker.reason: The claim cites only TypeCollector.cs lines 1008 and 1148 (the mixed-key continue statements), omitting the duplicate-key edits at lines 1023-1026, 1039-1042, 1163-1166, and 1179-1182, and the named test DuplicateKeysAreReportedWithoutAnalyzerFailureForGeneratedTypes (SuppressSourceGenerationAnalyzerTests.cs lines 147-166) uses two [Key(0)] properties (duplicate int keys), exercising lines 1023-1026 and never executing either cited line 1008 or 1148.

findings.description: Claim C1 disputed: While TypeCollector.cs adds continue after reporting DoNotMixStringAndIntKeys in both the property loop (line 1008) and the field loop (line 1148), the sole named test MixedKeyKindsAreReportedWithoutAnalyzerFailure (SuppressSourceGenerationAnalyzerTests.cs lines 125-144) declares only two properties and zero fields, so the claimed field-collection path at lines 1145-1149 is never exercised by the named test (nor is the string-key-then-int-key branch).

Claim C2 disputed: All three named tests (SuppressSourceGenerationAnalyzerTests.cs lines 81-100, 103-122, and 147-166) declare only properties and no fields, so none of them test the cited field-collection guards at TypeCollector.cs lines 1163-1166 and 1179-1182; furthermore, the earlier duplicate-key diagnostic reporting for intMembers and fields is outside the diff hunks and unverified for fields.

Claim C6 disputed: The claim cites only TypeCollector.cs lines 1008 and 1148 (the mixed-key continue statements), omitting the duplicate-key edits at lines 1023-1026, 1039-1042, 1163-1166, and 1179-1182, and the named test DuplicateKeysAreReportedWithoutAnalyzerFailureForGeneratedTypes (SuppressSourceGenerationAnalyzerTests.cs lines 147-166) uses two [Key(0)] properties (duplicate int keys), exercising lines 1023-1026 and never executing either cited line 1008 or 1148.

Duplicate-keyed members are now silently dropped instead of throwing. reportDiagnostic is invoked with ?. so it may be null in some paths. If this code runs in the source generator with no diagnostic sink, a formatter could be generated that omits a member, where the build previously failed loudly. Verify that a diagnostic is always surfaced when this branch is taken.

No hunk touches SuppressSourceGeneration handling. The fix only prevents crashes on duplicate or mixed keys, which affect all types. If the 3.1.1 regression was an early return or skip for suppressed types, it may not be fixed. Confirm that MemberWithoutKeyIsReported, AllowPrivateRequiredIsReported and MemberTypeMustBeMessagePackObjectIsReported failed before this change, or that the original repro case was duplicate keys.
The README states MsgPack012 (type accessibility) is still reported for suppressed types, but no new test covers MsgPack012 for a suppressed type.

The new 'continue' skips the rest of the loop body for the mismatched member. That means later per-member processing (formatter attribute lookup, hiddenIntKey increment) no longer runs for it. This only matters on the error path, but it changes what other diagnostics may be reported for that member.

README.md line 1623 states that for [MessagePackObject(SuppressSourceGeneration = true)], no formatter is generated and the type is serialized at run time by the dynamic resolvers, yet concludes 'so such a type remains AOT-safe.' This contradicts lines 1617-1618 and SuppressedSourceGenerationTests.cs line 23: because no precompiled formatter is generated and DynamicObjectResolver relies on Reflection.Emit at run time, a suppressed type without a manually supplied custom formatter will fail at run time in AOT environments (such as NativeAOT, iOS, or Unity IL2CPP) where dynamic code generation is unsupported.

When a property (line 1035) or field (line 1175) has a duplicate string key, TypeCollector does not continue early as it does for mixed keys; it still constructs MemberSerializationInfo and increments hiddenIntKey++ before lines 1039-1042 and 1179-1182 skip adding the member to stringMembers. Because TypeCollector is also invoked by the source generator (reportDiagnostic is nullable), any subsequent valid string-keyed member receives a non-contiguous IntKey (for example 0, 2 for 2 entries in stringMembers) instead of dense 0..Count-1 indices, risking out-of-range indexing or malformed code generation during IDE/build runs on code with duplicate string keys.
